title: Bridgewell Homeowner Service Contracts Cancellation: Notice, Credit and Refund
content:
## Clauses

**C1 — Notice and confirmation.** A cancellation of a Homeowner Service Contract starts when the customer gives notice: the agent records the notice on a cancellation request whose notice date is the date the customer gives notice, and the customer then confirms it. A contract is cancelled only after the customer has confirmed the cancellation request on file.

**C2 — Effective date.** The cancellation is effective on the notice date and is never backdated before it. The cancellation credit is computed as of the notice date.

**C3 — Free-look period.** The free-look period covers a notice given within the free-look period's calendar days after the start date, counted from the day after the start date with the boundary day included, and applies only in the first term. Within the free-look period the credit is all premium paid for the current term less the benefit Bridgewell has paid in the term, and no admin fee applies.

**C4 — After the free-look period.** An annual-billed contract is credited the unearned share of premium paid for the current term (the premium paid times the unexpired term days divided by the term days, rounded to the cent), less the cancellation administrative fee, less the benefit Bridgewell has paid in the term. A monthly-billed contract is credited nothing for installments already billed, is charged no admin fee, and is billed no further installments.

**C5 — Floor.** The credit is never negative: a result below zero is posted as a zero credit and the difference is not billed to the customer. Service call fees are never returned through a cancellation.

**C6 — Posting.** A cancellation credit is posted only after the customer has confirmed the cancellation request on file. Only one cancellation credit and one refund are posted per cancellation request. The credit is first applied to unpaid premium for periods before the notice date, and any credit balance left is refunded to the original payment method within the refund processing window (calendar days) after the cancellation is confirmed.

## Quantities used, as of the notice date

| Quantity | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Days since start | calendar days from the day after the original start date through the notice date inclusive |
| Premium paid for the current term | payments posted from the term start date through the notice date, less returned-payment charges billed in that span |
| Unexpired term days | calendar days from the day after the notice date through the term end date inclusive (zero when the notice date is on or after the term end date) |
| Term days | calendar days from the term start date through the term end date inclusive |
| Benefit paid in the term | every repair, replacement, supplemental allowance, cash-in-lieu and out-of-network payment on the contract whose service request falls in the term, less reversals of those authorizations |

## Worked examples (hypothetical; 30-day free look; 50.00 admin fee)

1. *First term, notice on day 20 after the start date, 863.89 paid, 300.00 benefit paid.* Within the free look: 863.89 less 300.00 gives a 563.89 credit, no admin fee.
2. *Annual-billed, notice after the free look, 863.89 paid, 146 of 365 days unexpired, no benefit paid.* 863.89 times 146 divided by 365 is 345.556, rounded 345.56; less 50.00 gives 295.56.
3. *Same as example 2 but 400.00 benefit paid.* 345.56 less 50.00 less 400.00 is below zero, so a zero credit is posted and nothing is billed.
4. *Monthly-billed, notice after the free look.* Credit zero, no admin fee, no further installments.
5. *Second term, notice ten days after the term start.* The free look applies only in the first term, so the after-free-look clause governs.

## Boundary of the free look (hypothetical start date May 1)

Notice on May 31 is day 30 and is within the free look; notice on June 1 is day 31 and is not.
